correctness.rationale: With α,β>0, q=β/α>0, and 0≤ρ≤1 (current endpoints by continuity), substitution of R_q(s)=s(1+qs)/(1+2s+qs²) gives a positive increasing bijection s>0 to ρ∈(0,1). Direct rational differentiation gives j′_q(s)=−qsP_q(s)/[(1+s)²(1+qs)²(1+2s+qs²)²]. All coefficients of P_q have exactly one + to − sign change in descending degree, and P_q(0)<0<P_q(∞), proving exactly one global maximizer. Scaling roots by s=u/q as q↓0 and s=q^(-1/3)u as q→∞ yields the limiting polynomials u³(u²−2) and u²(u³−2), respectively; sign bracketing plus uniqueness gives both root limits. Rational expansion yields the stated density and current coefficients. The q(1−ρ) boundary layer follows from the limiting positive quadratic root, including ξ=0. Packaged verify.py checked symbolic identities, both singular polynomials, and independent numerical bisections. No finite experiment substitutes for Descartes or asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: The throughput-optimal loading fraction is intrinsic to the proposed two-stage transport model. The source only shows its qualitative shift and the pointwise strong-recovery limit; the present theorem uniquely determines optimal density for every rate ratio and proves a sharp nonuniform q^(-1/3) saturation with constants and a distinct q^(-1) jamming boundary layer. These are quantitatively useful when tuning cooperative recovery and distinguish optimizing from holding density fixed, without imposing an arbitrary finite slice or demanding a downstream theorem.
